heard: The United States once ignored a fine for littering across Australia. Many believe America's first space station, Skylab, was safely steered into the deep ocean. But in July 1979, the massive station plummeted through the atmosphere as a fireball. Controllers tried to guide it, but a miscalculation sent flaming debris raining over Western Australia. Large fragments crashed near the town of Aspirance, landing on private properties and roofs. Local officials weren't impressed and issued NASA a real $400 ticket for littering. NASA ignored the administrative bill for decades until a California radio show heard the story. In 2009, loyal listeners raised the cash and finally settled the astronomical debt.
